maria: heads up — p99 jumped to ~1.2s on prod after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. Not all hosts, looks like a subset in eu-west-1 :grimace:

kai: saw it in dashboards, thanks. Is that the kernel priority change that prefers fused-attn for <2048 tokens?

maria: yes. baseline kernels: fused-attn preferred -> fallback to generic on mismatch. I grabbed a perf trace for an affected request.

infra-bot: deploybot: kernel-selector v2.3 rolled to eu-west-1 at 2026-03-14T17:42Z :rocket:

devon: can you paste the trace?

maria: pasting snippet: 
```
TRACE: request_id=req-89af
seq_len=512 prefix_len=450 gen_tokens=180 total_tokens=1130
kernel_choice: fused-attn (attempt) -> mismatch at runtime -> fallthrough to generic_kernel
kv_cache: hit_ratio=0.62; active_entries=128k; eviction_ops=3.2/s
microbatch_size=8 (adaptive->8)
latencies: fused_attempt=95ms; generic_exec=1.05s; total=1.18s
```

olivia: interesting — fallback path costs most of it. Why did fused attempt mismatch?

kai: mismatch usually when sequence shapes change vs compile-time profile. fused-attn compiled for dense head dims + contiguous KV layout. If KV cache got fragmented it can fail runtime checks.

ben: do we have kernel selector logs? I want the runtime check failure reason.

maria: yes log: `selector: runtime_check_failed: kv_layout_misaligned (stride!=expected)`

devon: kv_layout_misaligned... that suggests some sessions have mutated attention masks or there was an off-path eviction causing stride change. Any recent KV eviction changes?

maria: we did change the session rewarm eviction heuristic last week (reduce sticky affinity to improve cold-start throughput).

olivia: could the eviction heuristic cause compaction that changes the memory alignment/stride of KV buffers?

kai: maybe. Our allocator sometimes defragments small segments into a larger slab with different stride. If fused-attn requires packed KV we fail and expensive generic path used.

ben: load profile? Are affected requests long prompt ones or tool-call ones?

maria: mostly long-prompt + intermittent tool-calls. Tool-calls seem to make it worse: saw loops where a tool call chain expands tokens then returns and causes re-entry with different prefix length.

devon: that matches: tool-call returns new tokens that change subsequent generation windows; KV cache prefix+gen shape flips. Kernel selector uses static canonical shapes per model instance; sudden shape changes -> fallback.

maria: i also grabbed histograms. p50=120ms, p95=340ms, p99=1.18s (tail is all those fallback cases).

kai: two-pronged fix: 1) make fused-attn runtime checks more permissive (accept stride variants if semantically equivalent), 2) reduce allocator compaction during hot sessions or pin KV layout for session affinity.

olivia: permissive checks risk silent correctness issues — need test harness. Could we instead synthesize a microbench that reproduces stride mismatch?

maria: reproduced locally with this script: 
```
# repro: allocate kv slabs then trigger compact
python tools/repro_kv_stride.py --model llama-13b --prefix 450 --gen 180 --compact-after 2
```
Output: `runtime_check_failed: kv_layout_misaligned` -> generic kernel path taken

ben: nice. What's the p99 if we raise microbatch ceiling from 8 -> 12 for these hosts? More batching could amortize generic kernel cost?

kai: tested in staging: microbatch 8 -> 12 drops tail from 1.18s -> 900ms for same QPS, but p50 increases slightly. Throughput improves but latency SLO tighter at p95 so tradeoff.

devon: maybe smarter route: detect stride-mismatch and rebind to a compiled compatible kernel variant rather than generic. Shipping a secondary compiled kernel with looser layout constraints might be best.

olivia: ops ask: can we avoid allocator compaction for sessions flagged as "longprompt+toolchain"? We could set session flag to pin KV buffers for duration of conversation.

maria: yes we can. Proposal: session.flag preserve_kv_layout on toolcall entry; allocator skip compaction; TTL=15m.

ben: quick mitigation: roll back the eviction heuristic change for eu-west-1 and bump microbatch ceiling for affected hosts. Then schedule engineering fix: compile relaxed-kernel variant + add session pin.

kai: I'll open a PR for relaxed-kernel compile and add unit tests for stride variants. devon can you scope allocator change?

devon: on it. I'll add an integration test that runs toolcall loops and checks selector path never falls back.

infra-bot: incident: p99-spike-eu-west-1 created by maria at 2026-03-15T08:11Z (severity: P2) :eyes:

maria: thanks all. I'll run a targeted canary for the rollback and microbatch bump now, and attach traces to the incident. :thumbsup:

kai: good plan. follow-up: create perf regression guard in CI to catch kernel-selector runtime_check failures (fail build if >0 occurrences in perf run).

maria: adding to backlog and will post PR link in the incident thread.

olivia: small note — add a metric for `selector.runtime_check_failed.count` with tag kv_layout to alert earlier.

maria: done. will monitor for 24h and report back. :mag:
